s0201.literal: On dingsi day the army went out from Nan Province and burned the rebels' boats and ships.
s0201.idiomatic: On dingsi day the imperial troops marched out of Nan Province and burned the rebel fleet.

s0202.literal: On jiwei day Liu Guiyi, Xu Siyan, and Fu Yenang were beheaded in the Jiankang market.
s0202.idiomatic: On jiwei day Liu Guiyi, Xu Siyan, and Fu Yenang were executed in the market at Jiankang.

s0203.literal: Editorial footnote marker 22. That day martial law was lifted.
s0203.idiomatic: See editorial note 22. That day the capital stood down from martial law.

s0204.literal: On gengshen day Xiao Gui, Dongfanglao, Wang Jingbao, Li Xiguang, and Pei Yingqi all suffered execution.
s0204.idiomatic: On gengshen day Xiao Gui, Dongfanglao, Wang Jingbao, Li Xiguang, and Pei Yingqi were all put to death.

s0205.literal: The Founder memorialized to relinquish South Xuzhou and grant it to Hou Andu.
s0205.idiomatic: The Founder asked leave to give up South Xuzhou and turn it over to Hou Andu.

s0206.literal: In the seventh month, on jingzi day, an edict appointed the Founder Director of the Secretariat, Minister over the Masses, and Inspector of Yangzhou; advanced his rank to Duke; added to his fief, together with the previous grant, five thousand households; and left unchanged his posts as Palace Attendant, bearer of the staff, Commander-in-Chief of all armies at home and abroad, General, Director of the Masters of Writing, attendance retinue, pipes and drums, armor and weapons, as before—also granting an oil-canopied carriage with black wheels.
s0206.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on jingzi day, an edict named the Founder Director of the Secretariat, Minister over the Masses, and inspector of Yangzhou, raised him to duke, and added five thousand households to his fief on top of what he already held. He kept his palace attendant rank, staff of office, supreme command over all armies, generalship, directorship of the Masters of Writing, guard retinue, pipes and drums, and armor and arms as before, and was given an oil-canopied carriage with black wheels.

s0207.literal: That month Hou Chen submitted Jiang Province in allegiance.
s0207.idiomatic: That month Hou Chen brought Jiang Province over to the court.

s0208.literal: Hou Andu was sent to garrison the upper reaches and settle the southern interior commanderies.
s0208.idiomatic: Hou Andu was dispatched upstream to pacify the southern interior commanderies.

s0209.literal: In the eighth month, on guimao day, Grand Storehouse Director He Shu and Xin Province Inspector Hua Zhi each presented one jade seal; the Founder memorialized sending them to the terrace; an edict returned them to the Founder.
s0209.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on guimao day, Grand Storehouse Director He Shu and Xin Province Inspector Hua Zhi each offered a jade seal. The Founder sent them up to the throne; the court ordered them given back to him.

s0210.literal: That day an edict granted the Founder the revenue of Anji and Wukang, two counties together totaling five thousand households.
s0210.idiomatic: That same day an edict assigned him the tax income of Anji and Wukang—five thousand households in all.

s0211.literal: In the ninth month, on renyin day, the era name was changed to the first year of Great Peace.
s0211.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on renyin day, the reign was retitled the first year of Great Peace.

s0212.literal: The Founder was advanced to Chancellor, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Pacifying Grand General; the title inspector was changed to governor; he was further enfeoffed as Duke of Yixing commandery; Palace Attendant, Minister over the Masses, Commander-in-Chief, attendance retinue, pipes and drums, armor and weapons, and the black-wheeled carriage remained as before.
s0212.idiomatic: He was raised to chancellor, recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Pacifying Grand General; his Yangzhou post became a governorship; he was made Duke of Yixing. He kept his palace attendant rank, ministry, supreme command, guard retinue, pipes and drums, arms, and black-wheeled carriage unchanged.

s0213.literal: On dingwei day Palace Attendant for Scattered Retainers Wang Peng memorialized that on the fifth of this month at dawn he had seen dragon tracks on the imperial road from the Grand Altar of Soil and Grain to the Elephant Gate, strange for three or four li.
s0213.idiomatic: On dingwei day Wang Peng, palace attendant for scattered retainers, reported that at dawn on the fifth of the month he had seen dragon tracks along the imperial road from the Grand Altar to the Elephant Gate—a marvel stretching three or four li.

s0214.literal: On gengshen day an edict posthumously enfeoffed the Founder's father as Palace Attendant and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, with gold seal and purple sash, as Duke of Yixing, posthumous name Gong.
s0214.idiomatic: On gengshen day an edict posthumously ennobled the Founder's father as palace attendant and grand master for splendid happiness, with gold seal and purple sash, Duke of Yixing, posthumous name Gong.

s0215.literal: In the tenth month, on jiaxu day, an order said that from now on when the chancellor entered for audience he might use a separate couch placed near the imperial seat.
s0215.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on jiaxu day, the throne ordered that when the chancellor came in for audience he might sit on a separate couch beside the imperial seat.

s0216.literal: In the first month of the second year, on renyin day, the Son of Heaven received the myriad states at the Hall of Supreme Ultimate's eastern wing; the Founder's attendance retinue was increased by ten, his guard by thirty, the rest as before.
s0216.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year, on renyin day, the emperor received the tribute states in the eastern hall of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate. The Founder's ceremonial retinue was increased by ten and his guard by thirty; everything else stayed as it was.

s0217.literal: On dingwei day an edict posthumously enfeoffed the Founder's elder brother Daotan as Palace Attendant for Scattered Retainers, Editorial footnote marker 23. bearer of the staff, General Who Pacifies the North, Governor of Yan Province, and Duke of Changcheng, posthumous name Zhaolie;
s0217.idiomatic: On dingwei day an edict posthumously honored the Founder's elder brother Daotan as palace attendant for scattered retainers, See editorial note 23. bearer of the staff, General Who Pacifies the North, governor of Yan Province, and Duke of Changcheng, posthumous name Zhaolie;

s0218.literal: His younger brother Xiuxian as Palace Attendant, bearer of the staff, Rapid Tiger General, Governor of South Xuzhou, and Marquis of Wukang, Editorial footnote marker 24. posthumous name Zhongzhuang, each with a fief of two thousand households.
s0218.idiomatic: his younger brother Xiuxian as palace attendant, bearer of the staff, Rapid Tiger General, governor of South Xuzhou, and Marquis of Wukang, See editorial note 24. posthumous name Zhongzhuang, each with a fief of two thousand households.

s0219.literal: Editorial footnote marker 25. On jiayin day the concurrent Palace Attendant and Master of Ceremonial for the Heir Apparent Lu Zhan was sent to invest Lady Zhang of Changcheng as Lady of the State of Yixing.
s0219.idiomatic: See editorial note 25. On jiayin day Lu Zhan, concurrent palace attendant and master of ceremonies for the heir apparent, was sent to invest Lady Zhang of Changcheng as lady of the state of Yixing.

s0220.literal: On dingmao day an edict posthumously enfeoffed the Founder's grandfather as Palace Attendant and Minister of Ceremonial, posthumous name Xiao.
s0220.idiomatic: On dingmao day an edict posthumously honored the Founder's grandfather as palace attendant and minister of ceremonial, posthumous name Xiao.

s0221.literal: The Founder's grandmother Lady Xu was posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of Jiaxing county, Wu commandery, posthumous name Jing;
s0221.idiomatic: His grandmother Lady Xu was made Lady of Jiaxing in Wu commandery, posthumous name Jing;

s0222.literal: His mother Lady Zhang as Grand Lady of the State of Yixing, posthumous name Xuan.
s0222.idiomatic: and his mother Lady Zhang as Grand Lady of the State of Yixing, posthumous name Xuan.

s0223.literal: In the second month, on gengwu day, Xiao Bo raised troops, crossed the ranges from Guangzhou, halted at Nankang, and sent his generals Ouyang Hui, Fu Tai, and his son Zi as the vanguard, Editorial footnote marker 26. reaching Yuzhang and posting troops at strategic passes; South Jiangzhou Inspector Yu Xiaoxiang raised troops in response to Bo; the Founder ordered Zhou Wenyü and Hou Andu to lead the army to crush them.
s0223.idiomatic: In the second month, on gengwu day, Xiao Bo rebelled, crossed the mountains from Guangzhou, and camped at Nankang. He sent Ouyang Hui, Fu Tai, and his son Zi ahead, See editorial note 26. as far as Yuzhang, where they held the passes. Yu Xiaoxiang, inspector of South Jiangzhou, rose to join him. The Founder sent Zhou Wenyü and Hou Andu with an army to put the revolt down.

s0224.literal: In the eighth month, on jiawu day, the Founder was advanced to Grand Tutor, with the yellow battle-axe added, sword and shoes in the hall, no need to hurry in court, and no personal name spoken when he was praised in obeisance; he was also granted one set of feather-canopied pipes and drums; his Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Pacifying Grand General, Governor of Yangzhou, Dukedom of Yixing, attendance retinue, armor and weapons, and oil-canopied carriage with black wheels remained as before.
s0224.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jiawu day, he was made Grand Tutor and given the yellow battle-axe, the right to wear sword and shoes in the hall, to enter court without hurrying, and to be hailed without his personal name. He received a feather-canopied pipe-and-drum guard. He kept his palace attendant rank, supreme command, recordership, Pacifying Grand General post, Yangzhou governorship, Yixing dukedom, guard retinue, arms, and oil-canopied black-wheeled carriage unchanged.

s0225.literal: On jingshen day front and rear feather-canopied pipes and drums were added for the Founder.
s0225.idiomatic: On jingshen day he was given feather-canopied pipes and drums for his van and rear as well.

s0226.literal: At this time Xiang Province Inspector Wang Lin held troops and would not obey orders; the Founder sent Zhou Wenyü and Hou Andu leading the army to attack him.
s0226.idiomatic: At that time Wang Lin, inspector of Xiang Province, kept his army and refused orders. The Founder sent Zhou Wenyü and Hou Andu with troops against him.

s0227.literal: In the ninth month, on xinchou day, an edict said:
s0227.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on xinchou day, an edict ran:

s0228.literal: In ancient times when the primordial embryo was split apart and the great simplicity was still misty, to raise up the human sovereign one had to rely on a great minister.
s0228.idiomatic: When the world was first cleft from chaos and the great simplicity still hung as mist, to set up the human sovereign always required a great minister at his side.

s0229.literal: Therefore after worthy sages, regional lords were commissioned in the four quarters; among divinely martial rulers, a great overseer governed the myriad states.
s0229.idiomatic: After the sage kings came, lords were sent to rule the four quarters; under the most martial emperors, a great overseer governed all beneath heaven.

s0230.literal: Again there were those who with one correction united the realm—at the Gate of the Canal the gift was made lofty; who with girdle slain and girdle warmed won the favor of the traveling palace—so in peril the steadfast are proven, in prosperity the bright shine forth: this is the same wind for a thousand ages, the unchanging way of a hundred kings.
s0230.idiomatic: There were also those who with a single stroke set the realm right—the gift at the Canal Gate was raised high; who slew the girdle and warmed the girdle won favor in the traveling palace. In danger the loyal stand firm; in good fortune they shine the brighter. That is the wind that blows alike through a thousand ages, the way no king may set aside.

s0231.literal: The Grand Tutor, Duke of Yixing, is accomplished in letters and martial in deed, sage and divine; by nature endowed with virtue, he brings peace to the black-headed people.
s0231.idiomatic: The Grand Tutor, Duke of Yixing, is learned and warlike, sage and divine; heaven-born in virtue, he gives peace to the common people.

s0232.literal: Long ago in a time of repose he was early entrusted by the court; he went far beyond the blue sea and joined Jiao and Yue to the great pole.
s0232.idiomatic: In days of peace he was early given the court's trust; he crossed the southern sea and bound Jiao and Yue to the imperial center.

s0233.literal: Editorial footnote marker 27. The imperial fortune was unmade; the written covenant went unheard; within China it was perishing; the omens of war gathered; the people wailed; they were like prisoners in a ruined pen; high heaven hung far off, and none could say where the limit lay.
s0233.idiomatic: See editorial note 27. Then the dynasty's fortune broke; the written covenant was never heard; China itself seemed lost; the signs of war piled up; the people wailed like captives in a broken fold; heaven stood far off, and no one could see an end.

s0234.literal: When obstruction ends, peace comes; the chief minister answered the age; he rescued what was about to collapse and pulled back what had already drowned; riding boats and treading chariots, bridging peril and floating the deep, he campaigned midway and utterly destroyed the rebel host.
s0234.idiomatic: When the worst had passed, peace returned; the chief minister met the hour; he saved what was falling and pulled back what had sunk; by boat and chariot, over bridges of peril and across the deep, he fought through the heartland until the rebel host was wiped out.

s0235.literal: By the time of Stone City and Gushu, marrow flowed and entrails trailed; with one gesture of command the six quarters were cleared and tranquil.
s0235.idiomatic: At Stone City and Gushu marrow ran and guts littered the ground; at a single command the six quarters were cleared and stilled.

s0236.literal: Therefore he brightly illumined the martial successor, winged the radiance of the central capital, avenged the fierce wrongs of the three queens, and swept away the great evils of the three spirits.
s0236.idiomatic: Thus he lit the martial heir, steadied the brilliance of the central capital, avenged the fierce wrongs done the three queens, and swept away the great evils of the three spirits.

s0237.literal: The terrace of Yao and the assistant of Yu never rose so high; the minister of Yin and the teacher of Zhou are not to be named in the same breath.
s0237.idiomatic: The ministers of Yao and Yu never climbed so high; the counselors of Yin and Zhou are not fit to be named beside him.

s0238.literal: Added to this were the remaining signs of overthrow and collapse; Jing and Chu fell in ruin; heaven and earth had no heart; the imperial carriage was cast aside; the five barbarians pressed in to devour; they contended for the Chinese realm; the eight directions were bound in knots and none could set things right; powerful ministers defied orders and deposed our young sovereign; he could only gaze on the soul of the infant lord of Zhou and willingly bear the shame of Ning Qing.
s0238.idiomatic: On top of that came the last signs of ruin: Jing and Chu collapsed; heaven and earth seemed heartless; the imperial carriage was abandoned; the five barbarians pressed in to devour the land; they fought over China; the eight directions were tied in knots and no one could save them; great ministers defied the throne and cast down our young emperor; he could only look upon the infant lord's ghost and swallow the shame of Ning Qing.

s0239.literal: With sword at the neck and hair bound, the road of pleading had no way through; stealing axes and fleeing blame, there was nowhere to hide the body.
s0239.idiomatic: Sword at the throat and hair bound, there was no road of appeal; stealing the axe and fleeing blame, there was nowhere left to hide.

s0240.literal: The Duke's divine troops came in a rush; in no day all was cleared; only I, feeble and ignorant, again received heaven's mandate.
s0240.idiomatic: The Duke's divine army came like a storm; in less than a day all was cleared; and I, feeble and ignorant, received heaven's mandate once more.

s0241.literal: This again is vast and boundless—there is no virtue by which to name it.
s0241.idiomatic: That too is vast beyond naming—no virtue can compass it.

s0242.literal: Added to this, trusting in loyalty and righteousness, he slaughtered those demonic rebels; he shook away the barbarian miasma of the Zhen region and ended the evil omens at Mount Kuaiji; at Panyu and Lize, in the northern marches and western suburbs, he destroyed the wicked bands until not one remained.
s0242.idiomatic: Moreover, leaning on loyalty and righteousness, he cut down demonic rebels; he shook the barbarian miasma from the Zhen region and ended the evil omens at Kuaiji; at Panyu and Lize, in the northern marches and western suburbs, he destroyed the wicked until none were left.

s0243.literal: Thus the lives of the myriad people—long or short—hang upon him; the foundation of all within the seas—rise or fall—depends upon him.
s0243.idiomatic: Thus the lives of the myriad people, long or short, hang upon him; the foundation of all within the seas, rise or fall, depends upon him.

s0244.literal: Thereupon punishments and rites were taught together; institutions had their rules; within and without were at peace; far and near were united as one—so that the yang light joined the moon's brilliance, bright emblems showed their radiance, birds rested in the courtyard galleries, embracing benevolence and holding faith; his great merit covered the thick earth and the great Way reached the dark heaven.
s0244.idiomatic: Then punishments and rites were taught together, institutions took their proper form, within and without were at peace, and far and near were one—so that sun and moon shared their light, bright signs shone forth, birds rested in the palace galleries bearing benevolence and faith; his great merit covered the thick earth and the great Way reached the dark heaven.

s0245.literal: From Fu Xi, Shen Nong, Yan Di, and Hao Xu onward, in ages when the ruler held the scroll and let his robes fall, no sage who succored the people has been like this.
s0245.idiomatic: From Fu Xi, Shen Nong, the Flame Emperor, and the Yellow Lord onward, in every age of rule by scroll and trailing robe, no sage who succored the people has matched this.

s0246.literal: To prepare the regalia and codify the mandate—Huan and Wen received it; to assist yin and yang—Xiao and Cao did not yield; yet never was merit higher than rushing in service while reward was thinner than for Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou; all the people surely harbor long expectation.
s0246.idiomatic: To ready the regalia and codify the mandate was the portion of Huan and Wen; to assist yin and yang, Xiao and Cao did not yield place—yet never was service greater than his while reward was slighter than Yi Yin's or the Duke of Zhou's; all the people surely wait in hope.

s0247.literal: Truly because the Duke in humility restrains himself and lowers his person in thought, the fine tally lingers and long sighs are added.
s0247.idiomatic: Truly it is because the Duke restrains himself in humility and lowers his person in thought that the fine tally is delayed and sighs grow long.

s0248.literal: How can this lofty virtue be asserted and court design long left idle? The Director of Merit should be warned to reverently raise the great statute.
s0248.idiomatic: How can such lofty virtue be left unhonored and court design long idle? Let the Director of Merit be charged to raise the great statute in reverence.

s0249.literal: Moreover the great sage of Chonghua—at Guirui only the worthy were chosen; the sacrifices of great virtue must not be forgotten; the gate of duke and marquis must be restored.
s0249.idiomatic: The great sage Chonghua chose the worthy at Guirui; the rites of great virtue must not be forgotten; the gate of duke and marquis must be opened again.

s0250.literal: Therefore Yin praised Danfu and continued Hou Ji's office; Yao appointed Xi and He to inherit Chong Li's post.
s0250.idiomatic: Thus Yin praised Danfu and continued Hou Ji's office; Yao appointed Xi and He to inherit Chong Li's post.

s0251.literal: How much more when his own branch is established—should he not swear the covenant of river and mountain?
s0251.idiomatic: How much more when his own house is founded—should he not swear the covenant of river and mountain?

s0252.literal: Let him be advanced to Chancellor of State, head of the hundred officials, enfeoffed as Duke of Chen over ten commanderies, granted the full rites of the Nine Bestowals, with seal ribbon, far-wandering cap, and green sash added; his rank shall be above all princes and kings; his Pacifying Grand General and Governor of Yangzhou shall remain as before.
s0252.idiomatic: Let him be raised to chancellor of state, head of the hundred officials, enfeoffed as Duke of Chen over ten commanderies, and granted the full Nine Bestowals, with seal ribbon, far-wandering cap, and green sash; his rank shall stand above all princes and kings; he shall keep his Pacifying Grand General post and Yangzhou governorship unchanged.

s0254.literal: Great is the Qian origin, sustaining sun and moon for constant observation; utmost is the Kun origin, bearing mountains and rivers to carry the myriad things.
s0254.idiomatic: Great is the origin of Qian, sustaining sun and moon for the constant gaze; utmost is the origin of Kun, bearing mountains and rivers to carry the myriad things.

s0255.literal: Therefore only heaven is great—he who ascends to match it is reverently bright; only the king establishes the state—he who wings it is equal in holiness.
s0255.idiomatic: Only heaven is great, and he who rises to match it is reverently bright; only the king founds the state, and he who wings it is equal in holiness.

s0256.literal: Thus the assistants of Wen and Wu hid their jade scepters at Panxi; the ministers of Yao and Shun carved their golden tablets at Glory River.
s0256.idiomatic: Thus the aides of Wen and Wu hid jade scepters at Panxi; the ministers of Yao and Shun carved golden tablets at Glory River.

s0257.literal: How much more one whose form holds the unity of the great swan, who calms the peril of the yang ninth, who rescues the cross-flow at Jieshi and beats out the blaze-fire at Kunlun, who drives before him Wei and Peng and tramples Qi and Jin—whose divine merit moves yet is not employed, whose holy way runs yet has no name?
s0257.idiomatic: How much more one who embodies the unity of the great swan, who stills the peril of the ninth yang, who rescues the cross-flow at Jieshi and beats out the blaze at Kunlun, who drives Wei and Peng before him and tramples Qi and Jin—whose divine merit moves yet goes unused, whose holy way runs yet bears no name?

s0258.literal: Now I shall confer upon the Duke the canonical document; reverently hear my command:
s0258.idiomatic: Now I confer upon the Duke the canonical document. Hear my command in reverence:

s0259.literal: Lately high heaven did not pity; disorder struck our state; the net leaked and swallowed the boat; strong barbarians grew fierce within; the vast universe, the trembling black-headed people—of round heads and square feet, not one in ten thousand was spared; the Great Clarity was blocked and the pain at Bridge Mountain was already deep; the great treasure was hard pressed and the disaster at Pingyang followed in turn.
s0259.idiomatic: Lately heaven did not pity us; disorder struck the state; the net tore and the great fish escaped; strong barbarians raged within; in the vast universe the people trembled—of all who walked the earth, not one in ten thousand was spared; the Great Clarity was blocked and grief at Bridge Mountain ran deep; the great treasure was beset and disaster at Pingyang followed close behind.

s0260.literal: The chief minister answered the fortune, brought peace to the myriad people, drilled troops south of Lake Dian, raised banners north of Gui Ridge, hung the three lights where they had fallen, stilled the four seas where they flew in rebellion, slaughtered the owl-demon in the central land, and cut the whale in the misty ford.
s0260.idiomatic: The chief minister met the hour, saved the myriad people, drilled troops south of Lake Dian, raised banners north of Gui Ridge, hung up the three lights where they had fallen, and stilled the four seas in revolt; he slaughtered the owl-demon in the central land and cut the whale in the misty ford.

s0261.literal: He swept and settled the upper state and brightly opened the restoration.
s0261.idiomatic: He swept the upper realm clean and brightly opened the restoration.

s0262.literal: This then is the Duke's great creation for the imperial house.
s0262.idiomatic: This is the Duke's great creation for the imperial house.

s0263.literal: Thereafter heaven did not yet repent the calamity; barbarian fiends pressed in again; South Xia surged in collapse; the western capital was overthrown; rebel barbarians burned bright; seizing disorder they took their chance; they pushed in branch princes and stole the sacred vessel; the usurper minister darkened the rudder and drew in enemy foes by the side; already degraded to the Tung Palace, they then plotted peril for the Han gate; the imperial fortune was already in peril—how different from a dangling tassel; China shook—more than a tottering tile.
s0263.idiomatic: Yet heaven had not yet turned from the calamity; barbarian fiends pressed in again; the south collapsed in turmoil; the western capital was overthrown; rebel barbarians flared bright, seizing chaos for their chance; they pushed in princes of the blood and stole the sacred vessel; the usurper minister darkened the helm and drew enemies in at his side; already cast down to the Tung Palace, they then plotted peril at the Han gate; the imperial fortune was at the edge—no mere dangling tassel; China shook—worse than a tottering tile.

s0264.literal: The Duke in majesty flung up his sleeves, rescued and righted the native dynasty, restored Ju for Qi's capital, and pacified the Rong for the royal house.
s0264.idiomatic: The Duke in majesty flung up his sleeves, rescued and righted the native dynasty, restored Ju for Qi's capital, and pacified the Rong for the royal house.

s0265.literal: Therefore I again received the precious succession, again tread the imperial seat, drew in the wind of Jianwu, and recounted and proclaimed the odes of King Xuan.
s0265.idiomatic: Therefore I again received the precious succession and again took the imperial seat, drew in the wind of Jianwu, and recounted and proclaimed the odes of King Xuan.

s0266.literal: This again is the Duke's second creation for the imperial house.
s0266.idiomatic: This again is the Duke's second creation for the imperial house.

s0267.literal: When the Duke first took up affairs and first entered office, the Three Rivers and Five Ridges—none did he not look upon; silver caves and pearl palaces—wherever he went, peace.
s0267.idiomatic: When the Duke first took up affairs and first entered office, of the Three Rivers and Five Ridges there was none he did not survey; silver caves and pearl palaces—wherever he went, peace followed.

s0268.literal: Sun and Lu began strife; the Yue Mo became disaster; the southern tribes were on the brink and about to perish.
s0268.idiomatic: Sun and Lu began strife; the Yue Mo became disaster; the southern tribes teetered on the brink of ruin.

s0269.literal: Where the Duke's red banner pointed, demonic ramparts split open; where the white plume was barely waved, wicked bands crumbled to dust.
s0269.idiomatic: Where the Duke's red banner pointed, demonic ramparts split open; where the white plume barely stirred, wicked bands crumbled to dust.

s0270.literal: Were it not for his divine martial, the southern marches would long have been lost.
s0270.idiomatic: Without his divine martial power, the southern marches would long have been lost.

s0271.literal: This again is the Duke's merit.
s0271.idiomatic: This again is the Duke's merit.

s0272.literal: At the end of Great Unity, frontier government was not kept in repair; Li Ben ran mad and stole our Jiao and Ai, dared to take a great title, was more arrogant than Wei Tuo, held a chain of prefectures, and blazed more fiercely than Liang Shuo.
s0272.idiomatic: At the end of Great Unity the frontier was neglected; Li Ben ran mad, seized our Jiao and Ai, dared to take a royal title, outdid Wei Tuo in arrogance, held a chain of prefectures, and burned hotter than Liang Shuo.

s0273.literal: The Duke with heroic stratagem swept like lightning and wind, drove tower ships and crossed the blue sea straight; Xinchang and Dianche, Editorial footnote marker 28. all the hardship was endured; Suli and Jianing were wholly made into victory mounds.
s0273.idiomatic: The Duke with heroic stratagem swept like lightning and wind, drove tower ships and crossed the blue sea; at Xinchang and Dianche, See editorial note 28. every hardship was borne; Suli and Jianing were wholly heaped into victory mounds.

s0274.literal: The liao caves of Three Mountains and the barbarian corners of Eight Angles—far is the land of water dwellings, long the nation of fire mountains; where Ma Yuan never arrived, where Tao Huang never heard—none did not fear our kingly awesomeness, contend to attend the frontier post, return tribute to the heavenly storehouse, and present registers to the Grand Herald.
s0274.idiomatic: The liao caves of Three Mountains and the barbarian corners of Eight Angles—far lie the water dwellings, long the fire mountains; where Ma Yuan never came, where Tao Huang never heard—none failed to fear our kingly awesomeness, strive to attend the frontier post, send tribute to the heavenly storehouse, and present registers to the Grand Herald.

s0275.literal: This again is the Duke's merit.
s0275.idiomatic: This again is the Duke's merit.

s0276.literal: From the time the bandit foe overran the Yangzi, the palace quarters suffered dark insult.
s0276.idiomatic: From the time the bandit foe overran the Yangzi, the palace quarters suffered dark insult.

s0277.literal: The Duke slept on his spear and tasted gall, took his guard in hand and beat his breast; his spirit surged to the blue sky and flew to the purple gate.
s0277.idiomatic: The Duke slept on his spear and tasted gall, took his guard in hand and beat his breast; his spirit surged to the blue sky and flew to the purple gate.

s0278.literal: The Panyu commander-in-chief was by origin of the various Yi; when words won him comrades, he cherished the same evil.
s0278.idiomatic: The Panyu commander-in-chief was by origin one of the Yi peoples; when words won him allies, he cherished the same evil.

s0279.literal: Trusting in this loyalty, the Duke seized the moment to crush and settle them; he seized the Pei magistrate and beat the war drums, pacified Xinye and held the saddle.
s0279.idiomatic: Trusting in this loyalty, the Duke seized the moment to crush and settle them; he seized the magistrate of Pei and beat the war drums, pacified Xinye and held the saddle.

s0280.literal: This again is the Duke's merit.
s0280.idiomatic: This again is the Duke's merit.

s0281.literal: When the age was first hard and the regions many in difficulty, fierce men of merit gates made rebellion on Mount Heng; soldiers pressed the moats and ponds; the army included the Yi liao.
s0281.idiomatic: When the age was first hard and the regions troubled, fierce men of merit houses rebelled on Mount Heng; soldiers pressed the moats and ponds; the army included the Yi liao.

s0282.literal: The Duke, because the state was robbed and the frontier alarmed, knew nothing he would not do; he soothed the allied states and executed their ugly kind; none but were startled like fish and scattered like birds, bound with face to the fore and heads hung up.
s0282.idiomatic: Because the state was robbed and the frontier alarmed, the Duke left nothing undone; he soothed the allied states and executed their ugly kind until all were startled like fish and scattered like birds, bound with faces to the fore and heads hung up.

s0283.literal: The black-headed people of the southern land again secured rest and breath.
s0283.idiomatic: The people of the southern land again secured rest and breath.

s0284.literal: This again is the Duke's merit.
s0284.idiomatic: This again is the Duke's merit.

s0285.literal: Long driving the mountain ranges, he dreamed of the capital region; along the road the tribal chiefs in succession became brambles and barriers; Lu Yangqu led the command and wholly held the great metropolis; he gathered runaways and was just plotting obstruction and disorder; a hundred towers did not fight—what cloud ladders had not yet spied; ten thousand crossbows together drew—what high ramparts they could not overcome.
s0285.idiomatic: Long driving the mountain ranges, he dreamed of the capital; along the road tribal chiefs in turn became brambles and barriers; Lu Yangqu held command and wholly possessed the great metropolis; he gathered fugitives and plotted obstruction and disorder; a hundred towers would not yield—no cloud ladder had yet spied them; ten thousand crossbows drew as one—no high rampart could stand before them.

s0286.literal: The Duke with dragon stride and tiger step, Editorial footnote marker 29. roaring at wind and cloud, made mountains crumble and strong walls, the wilds without a stubborn formation; he cleared demonic miasma at Ganshi and extinguished evil vapor at Yudu.
s0286.idiomatic: The Duke with dragon stride and tiger step, See editorial note 29. roaring at wind and cloud, made mountains crumble and strong walls fall, the wilds without a stubborn line; he cleared demonic miasma at Ganshi and extinguished evil vapor at Yudu.

s0287.literal: This again is the Duke's merit.
s0287.idiomatic: This again is the Duke's merit.

s0288.literal: Qian Shi, a vicious criminal, held fast at Da Ao; the army begging life resembled Ma Teng's host; the floating people were many like Du Tao's troops; they pushed the spearhead and turned the hill, from north toward south; year after year they were punished—truly a fierce foe.
s0288.idiomatic: Qian Shi, a vicious outlaw, held Da Ao; his host of desperate men rivaled Ma Teng's bands, his drifting multitudes Du Tao's troops; they drove the spearhead and wheeled through the hills from north to south; year on year the court struck at them—yet they were a fierce foe indeed.

s0289.literal: The Duke sat wielding the three stratagems and controlled the six wonders from afar; righteous courage shared one heart; the pixiu exerted their strength; thunder rushed and lightning struck; valleys were still and mountains empty; the commanderies had no alarm of dogs barking; the clustered shrines ceased the fox-cry robbers.
s0289.idiomatic: The Duke sat with the three stratagems in hand and the six wonders at his command; loyal valor moved as one; his shock troops threw their full strength; thunder rushed and lightning struck until valleys fell silent and mountains emptied; no district heard the dog's bark of alarm; the hill shrines went still of fox-fire robbers.

s0290.literal: This again is the Duke's merit.
s0290.idiomatic: This again is the Duke's merit.

s0291.literal: The royal army attacked the bandit foe and next reached the sunken waves; weapons lacked double stores and the soldiers had the color of hunger.
s0291.idiomatic: The royal army attacked the bandit foe and next reached the sunken waves; weapons lacked double stores and the soldiers wore hunger on their faces.

s0292.literal: The Duke turned his banner at Lize, piled grain at Baqiu; the ode of the hundred thousand granaries was rich; the welcome of pot and drink was the army; military and civil transport by water never knew the difficulty of the pillar stone; ships and boats looked upon one another like moving the storehouse of Ao; rhinoceros channels and shell armor disdained thunder; high ships and layered towers touched the sky; therefore the three armies were brave and sharp, a hundred battles without a forebear; relying on this army grain, they then destroyed the vicious rebels.
s0292.idiomatic: The Duke turned his banner at Lize and piled grain at Baqiu until the ode of the hundred thousand granaries rang full; pots and drink lined the army's road; grain moved by water without the pillar stone's hazard; ships passed like shuttling Ao's storehouse; rhinoceros channels and shell armor disdained thunder; high ships and tiered towers scraped heaven—so the three armies grew fierce and unbeaten; on that grain they destroyed the vicious rebels.

s0293.literal: This again is the Duke's merit.
s0293.idiomatic: This again is the Duke's merit.

s0294.literal: As for heroic design surpassing custom, righteous hosts like clouds—at Pen rampart suspicion and division delayed the military plan.
s0294.idiomatic: As for heroic design surpassing custom and righteous hosts like clouds—at Pen rampart suspicion and division delayed the military plan.

s0295.literal: The Duke's will was only to share the same breath; the army overcame through harmony; the swan pass was not feared; the Hong Gate was the meeting—like the Jin marquis swearing at White Water, like the King of Xiao pushing the red heart; bowing in rite and joining in alliance, men and spirits were moved to sigh—therefore the naval army kept the road and far and near shared one heart.
s0295.idiomatic: The Duke's will was only to share the same breath; the army overcame through harmony; the swan pass was not feared; the Hong Gate was the meeting—like the Jin marquis swearing at White Water, like the King of Xiao offering the red heart; bowing in rite and joining alliance, men and spirits sighed with feeling—so the naval army held the road and far and near shared one heart.

s0296.literal: This again is the Duke's merit.
s0296.idiomatic: This again is the Duke's merit.

s0297.literal: Gushu was the throat of the pass; Xiaohan was the barrier of the defile; the bandit foe held its gates and bridges; great robbers bore its bolts and bars.
s0297.idiomatic: Gushu was the throat of the pass; Xiaohan was the barrier of the defile; the bandit foe held its gates and bridges; great robbers bore its bolts and bars.

s0298.literal: With one command the Duke judged and directed; the three heroes together exerted themselves; left worthy and right horn—sand collapsed and earth crumbled; wooden armor perished in the central land; barbarian fur went to the river waters; they pressed and pressed—myriad plans and thousand rebels; the narrow pass of Ese was opened; the road of Yigeng was unblocked.
s0298.idiomatic: With one command the Duke judged and directed; the three heroes strove together; left worthy and right horn—sand collapsed and earth crumbled; wooden armor perished in the central land; barbarian fur went to the river waters; they pressed and pressed—myriad plans and thousand rebels; the narrow pass of Ese was opened; the road of Yigeng was unblocked.

s0299.literal: This again is the Duke's merit.
s0299.idiomatic: This again is the Duke's merit.

s0300.literal: The righteous army's great troops all gathered at the imperial capital; the rebellious wicked and vicious bands still encamped in the imperial city.
s0300.idiomatic: The righteous army's great host gathered at the imperial capital; the rebellious wicked and vicious bands still encamped in the imperial city.
